summary.en-US: Open the current Firefox tab in Google Chrome with one click. Windows helper required. No tracking.

description.en-US:
One click. Your tab in Chrome.

Chrome Hop opens the current HTTP or HTTPS page in your installed Google Chrome on Windows 11, keeping your Firefox tab open. Pin the button to your Firefox toolbar and click it when you want to switch browsers. Localhost web pages work too.

A separate, free Windows helper is required. On the add-on’s setup page, click Download for Windows, open the downloaded installer and follow the steps. View on GitHub is a separate button for source and release details. Direct download: https://github.com/aspendesign/chrome-hop/releases/latest/download/ChromeHop-Setup-windows-x64.exe . Run it once for your Windows account. No administrator access or runtime downloads are needed. Google Chrome Stable must be installed in its normal Windows location.

Chrome Hop requests only activeTab and nativeMessaging. It has no content scripts, persistent website permissions, tab scanning, history/cookie access, telemetry, background service, custom executable command or shell. The standalone Go helper accepts only one validated HTTP(S) URL.

Privacy: clicking the button sends the selected address to the helper and Chrome on your computer. Mozilla classifies this local transfer as browsing activity. Chrome Hop does not store or log the address or send it to a developer server. Chrome loads the address normally using its own profile and settings; Firefox login sessions and page state are not copied.

Windows 11 x64, Firefox 142+ and Google Chrome Stable. Other operating systems, custom Chrome paths, Beta/Canary and other Chromium browsers are not supported in version 1. Independent open-source project; not affiliated with Mozilla or Google.

privacy_policy.en-US: Chrome Hop sends only the clicked tab’s HTTP(S) address to its native helper and installed Google Chrome on the same computer. The address may include a query string or token. Nothing happens until you click. The add-on and helper have no telemetry, accounts, analytics, URL logs or network requests. They do not copy cookies, passwords, browsing history, page content or Firefox sessions. The developer receives no product data. Chrome loads the address normally under its own privacy settings and may keep history or sync. Mozilla categorizes the local handoff as browsingActivity, which the manifest declares. GitHub and Mozilla handle visits, downloads, updates and voluntary reports under their own policies. Full policy: https://github.com/aspendesign/chrome-hop/blob/main/docs/PRIVACY.md

version.approval_notes: Windows 11 x64 only. This is a minimal MV3 activeTab/nativeMessaging toolbar action. No content scripts, host permissions, telemetry or network APIs. The clicked HTTP(S) URL is sent to native host io.github.aspendesign.chrome_hop, restricted to chrome-hop@aspendesign.github.io. Local URL handoff is disclosed as browsingActivity per current native-messaging policy. The standalone Go helper source, threat model, tests and per-user Inno Setup installer are public at https://github.com/aspendesign/chrome-hop. Install the helper from the matching GitHub release, pin the add-on toolbar button, open https://example.com/ and click. Chrome Stable opens the address; Firefox stays open. Without the helper, a packaged actionable help page opens. Raw extension files are human-readable and untransformed, with no bundling/minification. The icon is original. More details and artifact hashes are in the repository verification/ and release assets.
